rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Frosted Blooms 1.1 Game Play 1.2 Buildings 1.3 Each Round 1.4 Scoring Frosted Blooms This game comprises of tile laying and building improvements, which you can include by leaving spaces within your garden. Game Play Form clumps of of white flowers, purple flowers, tulips and watercourse. Each round, you choose an objective card from your hand to score. For example, if you've just added to a clump of purple flowers, then you might choose to score the purple flower card, giving you two points for each purple flower adjacent to the new additions. In addition to the objectives in your hand, there are group objectives available for the first player to reach them. Buildings Building a (vacant) 1x1 square gives a worker, 3pts and a coin. Building a (vacant) 2x1 square gives a barn and 10 points. Building a (vacant) 2x2 square gives a windmill and 25 points. The green circle with a question mark in the corner of your screen will explain buildings in more detail. Each Round Take the tile clockwise of the (pink) flower token. If you have coins, you may pay a coin for each tile you wish to step over. They will be collected by the player taking the tile Place your chosen tile within your starting garden, forming collections of white flowers, purple flowers, tulips and water. Choose which objective card you wish to score this round. Check the joint objectives available. (note that taking a lower point card in a category means you can't also take a higher one in that category as well). Scoring Buildings score at the end of the game, in addition to points from the objectives.

---

[Rating: 5/10] A nice surprise.  Very interesting in that it rewards you for willingly leaving holes on your board. Off the top of my head, I can't remember any game that does this.  Having a personal deck of scoring cards is another rather unique feature. You can plan around the 3 cards in your hand and plan even further ahead if you already know all of the cards in the deck.  If you want a nice family, tile-laying game or are curious about these features and you love this genre, I think it's worth trying it.

[Rating: 5/10] Frosted Blooms is a top-notch production of an solid polydomino-laying concept.  The glitch is big.  Players cannot begin assessing their tile purchase until the start of their turn.  The AP seems to add 3-4 minutes per turn (about a drudgerous hour to a 4-player game).  One solution? Give each player a hand of 3 polydominos.  After they play 1, they replace it with the replenishment step as defined.
